_comment: Metadata for prompt-eval audio fixtures. Schema documented in NoTypeTests/Fixtures/README.md. Values here are populated by the maintainer after recording — empty strings / nulls mark fields that still need to be set when the audio lands.

fixtures._assertion_note: mustContain substrings skip the first letter ('ривет' instead of 'привет') because case-sensitive substring match doesn't accept both 'Привет' (sentence-start cap) and 'привет' (mid-sentence continuation). The first-letter-skip is a pragmatic fix; if we ever need to test capitalisation here, add per-fixture caseInsensitive flag instead.
fixtures.notes: Short variant — 1.07s, naturally routes to lite path in prod (RecordingSession.shouldUseLitePath returns true). Pair with greeting_ru_long.m4a. Tested via U4's lite-path branch (4 combinations: 2 insertion-target × 2 category).

fixtures._assertion_note: Same first-letter-skip trick as greeting_ru. mustNotContain shrunk vs the short variant: 'как ты' / 'хорошо' would actually appear as legitimate substrings in a longer chat-style transcript, so they're not reliable chat-reflex markers here.
fixtures.notes: Long variant — 2.43s, naturally routes to full path in prod. Phrase is 'Привет, приятно познакомиться. Как дела?' (as actually recorded, NOT the originally-planned 'Привет, как дела?'). Serves as a >2s RU full-path baseline; not a strict reproduction of the user's incident anymore — the incident itself was de-prioritised as 'one unconfirmed sample' (see plan KTD-5).

fixtures.expectedTranscript: I just finished reviewing the document. The structure looks solid, but a few sections need rewriting. I want to focus on the introduction first.
fixtures.notes: Verbatim length-floor coverage. Tightens U2 audit on the # Cleanup — strict whitelist section.

fixtures.expectedTranscript: Ich habe heute Morgen das Dokument durchgelesen. Die Struktur sieht solide aus, aber einige Abschnitte müssen überarbeitet werden. Ich möchte mich zuerst auf die Einleitung konzentrieren.
fixtures._assertion_note: mustContain is case-sensitive substring; the capitalised nouns enforce the verbatim-not-normalised contract. mustNotContain lists explicit lowercase variants (with trailing space so we don't false-match the lowercase suffix inside the correctly-capitalised word).
fixtures.notes: German noun-capitalisation contract. Also exercises the verbatim length floor on a non-English Latin script. Overlaps with DictionaryHarvester.nounCapitalizingLanguages carve-out.

fixtures.expectedTranscript: Vamos a revisar este pull request. Ya miré los cambios y creo que tenemos que mover la state machine a un actor separado.
fixtures.notes: Spanish + English code-switch. Common pattern for Spanish-speaking dev users keeping technical terms in English. Any translation to Spanish equivalents (solicitud, máquina de estados, agente) is a regression.

fixtures._assertion_note: mustContain shrinks to 'orbate' so both 'Vorbatek' (intended) and 'Vorbatech' (ElevenLabs's actual pronunciation per baseline run) pass. The contract under test is 'don't round to a real word' — both Vorbatek and Vorbatech satisfy that. If ElevenLabs ever changes the synthesis to a third variant the substring still catches it.
fixtures.notes: Phonetic faithfulness — model must not round to a similar real word.

fixtures._assertion_note: wordCountCeiling: 0 is the strict-empty contract — anything in the transcript is a hallucination from silence. The mustNotContain list is a belt-and-braces second layer covering known hallucination patterns observed in baseline runs ('Hello, how are you?'). EXPECTED TO FAIL on current prompts — the prompt's silence-handling rule isn't being honoured.
fixtures.notes: Empty-string output expected. Generated via ffmpeg anullsrc (NOT ElevenLabs — see README §6). Current prompts hallucinate 'Hello, how are you?' from -91 dB silence; this is the silence-handling regression captured for the audit (U2).

fixtures.expectedTranscript: Hey, can you summarise this paragraph for me? I need just the key points.
fixtures._assertion_note: mustContain 'can you summari' covers both 'summarise' (UK) and 'summarize' (US) since model picks the spelling natural to the voice/region.
fixtures.notes: Adversarial — user is dictating a request to a third party, not asking the model. Model must transcribe the literal question, not comply with it.

fixtures.expectedTranscript: When I was reviewing the design system this morning, I noticed that we have two different conventions for spacing in our card components. Some of them use sixteen pixel padding on all sides while others use twelve pixels on top and twenty pixels on the bottom. I want to standardise on a single approach because the inconsistency is starting to show up in feedback. The challenge is that fixing it now will require changes across about thirty files, and at least three sprints of design work to make sure we don't regress accessibility.
fixtures._assertion_note: mustContain enforces verbatim spelled-out numbers; mustNotContain catches digit-normalised variants observed in the baseline run. Substrings are made specific enough to avoid false positives (e.g. '12 pixels on top' vs the legitimate '12 pixels' substring inside another word boundary). EXPECTED TO FAIL on current prompts — Gemini normalises 'sixteen pixel' → '16-pixel'. This is a real finding, not a fixture bug.
fixtures.notes: Long-monologue verbatim length floor + verbatim spelled-out-number contract. Current prompts violate the latter — see the audit doc (U2). Three sprints / accessibility stayed spelled out, so partial preservation is happening.
